label: Bible Study
prompt: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he _____: and God saw that it was good.
verse: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
note: Day three: God names the dry land and the gathered waters, then signs off with his favorite review — good.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be _____ thee.
verse: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.
note: Friends carried a paralyzed man to Jesus on a bed, and the first thing He gave him was forgiveness.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And suddenly there was a great _____, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
verse: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
note: At midnight in Philippi, an earthquake opened every prison door and loosed every prisoner's bands.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a _____ God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;
verse: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;
note: From the Ten Commandments: God's jealousy is a husband's claim on his covenant people, not petty envy.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and _____ as an army with banners?
verse: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
note: The beloved, fair as the moon and clear as the sun, is 'terrible as an army with banners' — awe-inspiring, not awful.
